Daybook now runs on Linux. Built and tried on Fedora 44; it should work on any recent 64-bit Linux. If you installed Daybook on Windows with the installer, the app offers this update by itself. Restart Daybook, or press **Settings → Updates → Check for updates**, to see it straight away.

## New: Linux

Two files, pick one:

- **`Daybook-1.4.4.x86_64.rpm`** for Fedora and other systems that use .rpm. It installs Daybook into the app menu like any other program. Double-click it and press **Install**, or in a terminal: `sudo dnf install ./Daybook-1.4.4.x86_64.rpm`. When a new version comes out, the update button opens this page: download the new .rpm and install it the same way.
- **`Daybook-1.4.4.AppImage`** runs without installing, on most Linux systems. Right-click it, open **Properties**, turn on **Executable as Program**, then double-click it. It updates itself, like the installed Windows app.

On Linux:

- **Settings → Desktop widget → Start when I log in** starts Daybook when you log in.
- GNOME does not show icons by the clock, so the menu there is out of reach. To bring back a hidden widget, start Daybook again from the app menu. To stop Daybook, use **Settings → Quit Daybook**.
- Your data stays on each computer. To bring your history from Windows: on Windows, **Settings → Your data → Export a backup**. On the laptop, **Restore from file**.

## Fixed

- **Switching the theme on Windows:** the window's buttons at the top right changed colour before the circle reached them. They now change as it arrives.

## Changed

- **Settings → Desktop widget** has **Quit Daybook**, and "Start with Windows" is now **Start when I log in**.

## Downloading

- **Windows:** `Daybook-Setup-1.4.4.exe` (installs, and updates itself) or `Daybook-1.4.4-portable.exe` (runs without installing). Windows will say *"Windows protected your PC"*. Press **More info → Run anyway**.
- **Mac:** `Daybook-1.4.4-mac.dmg`. The first time, macOS refuses to open it. Go to **System Settings → Privacy & Security** and press **Open Anyway** next to Daybook.
- **Linux:** see above.

The Windows and Mac warnings are about the missing paid signing certificates, not about the program. The source is all in this repository if you would rather build it yourself.
